playbook:
When asked to hide, I pick a cell with a simple randomizing rule biased away from any cluster: rotate among three nonadjacent cells (e.g., positions a, b, c) rather than always the center, and change the trio if opponents pattern around me.

When I see an opponent repeatedly target me, I move unpredictably between my three chosen cells rather than staying central or repeating the same cell.

When choosing a hiding cell after observing prior hides, I favor cells that opponents have not recently targeted to reduce hit probability.

When firing, I comply with the standing order for target identity, but I choose my fired cell based on the target’s observed hide frequency (pick their modal cell if one exists; else randomize among three cells avoiding obvious repeats).

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I report it exactly as given — I do not lie or attempt to game claim validation.

When Harbor is a legal target, I only fire at Harbor if the immediate point transfer (3 points to me) and strategic value outweigh the political cost; avoid shooting Harbor purely for spite or predictability unless I intend to be the aggressor.

When arranging escorts, I offer and accept mutual escort only with a player who has reliably reciprocated or who benefits enough to make mutual 5-point gains likely; if no reliable partner, claim none.

When posting a public station note, I use concise, actionable signals: report observed targeting patterns, state my intended hiding rotation, or announce willingness to form an escort pact; avoid vague mirroring talk.

When I notice opponents mirroring each other, I do not mirror them; instead I probe by deviating in low-cost ways (hide change, vote deviation, or a one-off escort) to detect alliances.

When votes, nominations, or other public actions are called for, I watch for consistent pairings; if two players repeatedly back each other, I treat them as allied and act to exploit or break that alliance as my position demands.

When my score is low and others are high, I prioritize creating opportunities for mutual escorts or targeting the leader with the best chance of hit (based on observed hides) rather than continuing passive mirroring.

When I have limited information about targets’ hide tendencies, I randomize my fired cell across three nonadjacent cells to avoid giving opponents an easy pattern to exploit.

When a shot at me is successful, I log the shooter’s last known target cell and be more likely to shift away from that cell on my next hide.

When the game forces public validation of coordinates and claims, I use that transparency to call out inconsistencies promptly; do not tolerate vague or unverifiable notes.

When an action clearly did not work in prior play (e.g., sustained mirroring produced no points and made me predictable), I stop mirroring and adopt probing deviations to gather information and seize scoring chances.

1.text:
When I must pick a hide cell, I vary between off-center and center to avoid predictability; do not repeat the same cell twice in a row unless a clear strategic reason exists.

When the standing order tells me which station to fire at, I follow the standing order unless the target is Harbor and I am willing to accept being jettisoned; otherwise do not fire on Harbor.

When I choose a firing coordinate, pick a cell that balances coverage (center for higher chance) and unpredictability (offset cells across rounds) rather than always the same cell.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I publicly claim exactly that result (the claim must match the office report).

When composing station notes, mirror cooperative language of presumed allies to avoid standing out, and explicitly state that I am watching nominations/votes; avoid aggressive accusations unless I have decisive information.

When other boats show coordinated messaging, mirror that coordination until I see evidence of betrayal; use mirroring to probe alignment through reactions to nominations/votes.

When an escort payoff is only possible if two boats name each other, claim an escort only if I reasonably expect reciprocity (e.g., prior mutual signals or explicit coordination); otherwise claim none.

When my score is substantially positive relative to others, avoid risky plays (e.g., attacking Harbor, needless exposure) and favor conservative hiding and claiming to protect the lead.

When my shot hits a rival and that yields a useful score swing, continue pressure on that station per standing order; when it misses, do not fake the claim and resume probing via notes and vote monitoring.

When considering attacking Harbor for the payroll, weigh immediate +3 vs guarantee of being removed by Harbor’s warning; do not attack Harbor unless the payoff of jettisoning myself (and forcing Harbor off) is strategically desired.

When votes/nominations are presented, record and report anomalies; use public notes to highlight deviations so I can identify coordination or betrayal among others.

Do not attempt to falsely report shot results (claims must match office); instead use hide choices, firing cell variation, note-mirroring, and selective escort claims as my levers.

2.text:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that avoids obvious patterns: vary between edges and interior, avoid repeating the same number twice in a row, and prefer cells away from where I see others consistently firing.

When given the standing firing order, follow it unless there is a clear, deliberate reason to break it; do not randomly override the standing order.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report that result honestly in the public claim (claim hit if told hit, claim miss if told miss).

When posting a station note, mirror the tone and basic content of cooperative players to signal alignment, then add one short line that probes for deviation (e.g., “I’ll mirror key voters; flag any deviations”) rather than inventing complex narratives.

When I want escort points, name only actual fleet boat names (no invented/neutral names). Only claim to have escorted a specific boat if I expect a reciprocal claim or if I can plausibly induce reciprocity via notes; otherwise claim none.

When two-way escort reciprocity is plausible, pursue it: use notes to explicitly suggest mutual escort and follow through to get the 5-point exchanges.

Do not fire on Harbor except as an explicit strategy to remove Harbor (understand that firing on Harbor forces jettison and transfers 3 points); treat Harbor as a protected/expensive target by default.

When choosing firing coordinates, balance unpredictability with hit probability: avoid always choosing the same “safe” number; bias shots toward center cells when trying to maximize hit chance but mix in off-center shots to avoid being predictable.

When my shot hits, use that public hit claim to build credibility for later reciprocal escort negotiations; when my shot misses, accept the credibility hit and use notes to restore alignment with others.

When others’ notes and nominations are consistent and cooperative, continue mirroring to maintain coalition and probe; when someone deviates in wording or voting, call out the deviation succinctly and adjust my mirror stance accordingly.

Do not name non-existent boats or out-of-scope labels in salvage/escort claims—this was ineffective and can be invalidated.

When no clear escort partner exists and reciprocity is unlikely, claim none rather than making a random claim that offers no benefit.

When the round sequence shows someone consistently hitting me or another ally, prioritize hiding pattern changes and coordinate via notes to either avoid their targeting pattern or to set up reciprocal escorts that offset losses.

When making any public message, keep it short, actionable, and consistent with my past claims to preserve credibility.
